Exhibit C TENANT DESIGN CRITERIA Nashville Farmers Market MARKET DESIGN CONCEPT The Nashville Farmers Market intends to remodel the interior of the Market’s main building. This project will require all merchants to submit design packages that conform to the following rules. Each package will be reviewed by the Market Board of Directors, Metro’s Real Property Services and the State of Tennessee. Each shop will be reviewed both independently and how it interacts with the shops surrounding it. Tenants are encouraged to develop bold and creative shop designs within a set framework that ensures a lively, almost entertaining atmosphere, but within the overall design of the Market. Shops should allow open and clear contact between the merchant and customer and generous and attractive display of all products. Designs that feature the production of a specific product are encouraged. Much of the visual excitement of the Market depends on the openness of each stand allowing simultaneous intimate and long views of the Market as a whole. Each shop must be laid out so that it is both an attractive statement in itself, but also a window that provides views to the Market that lay beyond that particular shop. The Markets goal is the effective display of the full range of merchandise, without clutter and confusion, while maintaining easy but secure access for both customer and merchant. The character of each shop should reinforce the basic product group it offers. A good design allows the merchandise to speak for itself, with customer sight-lines to product production if possible. This will increase the customer’s interest in the merchant’s product and a sense of excitement. Only durable design and materials will hold up under the usage experienced over the long term. Like any business investment, the shop should be seen as a capital asset that will retain its value only when planned and properly maintained. The optimum balance in the Market derives from individual shops that provide unity to the site as a whole while remaining unique. Compatibility with adjacent counters, signage and presentation must be taken into consideration and will be reviewed during the approval process.
